column1: # silvarbor.git_safety.worktree_isolated - ALLOWLIST-DEPENDENT cases only
# Format: <expected>\t<label>\t<command>     (TAB separated, exactly 3 columns)
#   expected : ALLOW or DENY
#   command  : the command line handed to `dcg explain`.
#              A literal \n in this column becomes a real newline.
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
# WHY ONLY SIX CASES ARE LEFT HERE
# The other 45 moved to tests/corpus/, which dcg evaluates natively via
# `dcg corpus` with rule_id assertions and baseline diffing.
# These six cannot move. `dcg corpus` evaluates PACK MATCHING and does not
# apply allowlist.toml. Each command below is blocked by a built-in core.git
# rule and is permitted only because ../allowlist.toml switches that rule off.
# Under corpus every one reports "deny"; against the live guard every one is
# ALLOW:
#   git reset --hard HEAD~1       corpus: deny (core.git:reset-hard)          live: ALLOW
#   git reset --merge             corpus: deny (core.git:reset-merge)         live: ALLOW
#   git checkout -- src/main.rs   corpus: deny (core.git:checkout-discard)    live: ALLOW
#   git restore src/main.rs       corpus: deny (core.git:restore-worktree)    live: ALLOW
#   git branch -d feature/x       corpus: deny (core.git:branch-force-delete) live: ALLOW
#   git branch -D feature/x       corpus: deny (core.git:branch-force-delete) live: ALLOW
# These are the charter's signature claims - the operations deliberately
# permitted because they cannot cross the worktree boundary. They are exactly
# the assertions the corpus cannot make, so they are tested here against
# effective policy. If allowlist.toml is ever trimmed, this suite fails while
# the corpus stays green.
ALLOW
ALLOW
ALLOW
ALLOW
ALLOW
ALLOW
